correctness.rationale: For all integers m>=3, averaging an arbitrary feasible symmetric stochastic matrix over dihedral automorphisms does not increase ||P-J||_2, so a two-edge-orbit optimum exists. Fourier characters give exact 2-by-2 eigenblocks; the nonconstant positive branch at delta is a lower bound for every invariant matrix. Increasing spoke probability lowers this bound until rim holding vanishes. Along the resulting capacity boundary every other mode is dominated by that positive branch, including negative and zero-frequency modes. The scalar objective is strictly convex with opposite endpoint derivative signs and its explicitly stated stationary radical has norm sqrt(delta)/2, proving exact global optimality and uniqueness among invariant matrices. Taylor expansion of the exact trigonometric parameter proves the stated asymptotic. The calculation and full spectra are corroborated by the included verifier, without using finite checks as an infinite proof.

originality.rationale: The closed formula solves the uniform-equilibrium fastest-mixing problem on all sunlet graphs C_m corona K_1, m>=3. The inspected foundational SDP paper establishes a general convex formulation, but not this graph-family answer. The inspected symmetry paper solves cycles and wheels and shows a different six-node-cycle bump graph only experimentally; these do not imply the sunlet allocation or its two-term asymptotic. A later full-text clique-lift and tree-subgraph study addresses distinct graph operations and subgraph structures, not a cycle carrying m separate leaves. Focused searches found no exact prior result in the accessible records. General algorithmic solvability is not equivalent to the present explicit theorem; residual specialized priority risk remains.

value.rationale: A naturally defined infinite family of non-edge-transitive networks admits a nontrivial all-sizes closed-form global fastest-mixing rule. Unlike a parameter sweep, the theorem identifies the unique dihedrally invariant weight allocation and an active constraint: every optimal invariant chain removes all rim holding. The pendant transition probability shrinks as a constant multiple of the inverse rim size, while the optimal SLEM gap has a two-term expansion a quadratic inverse-size leading term and an explicit cubic inverse-size correction; the attached leaves have a precise spectral design cost. These results answer a motivated graph-optimization question not implied by a numerical SDP listing.
